title: Characterizing Tumor Hypoxia With BOLD-MRI to Predict Y-90 Treatment Response
official: Characterization of the Hypoxic Tumor Microenvironment With Blood Oxygen Level-Dependent Magnetic Resonance Imaging for the Prediction of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Response to Yttrium-90 Selective Internal Radiation Therapy
summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether a special type of magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI), called blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) MRI, can help measure how much oxygen is present in liver tumors. Tumors with low oxygen levels are described as being hypoxic.

Yttrium-90 (Y-90) is a type of radioactive material used to treat liver tumors, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a type of liver cancer. Y-90 is a form of radiation treatment delivered directly to liver tumors through tiny beads carried by blood vessels. These beads release radiation that damages and kills cancer cells while helping limit radiation exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. This treatment is also called Y-90 radioembolization or selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT).

interventions.name: Blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI)

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Subjects must meet all the inclusion criteria to participate in this study.

* Adults ≥ 18 years
* Liver mass(es) suspected of being HCC by imaging and are amenable to undergo percutaneous liver mass biopsy to confirm the HCC diagnosis, as determined by the institutional multidisciplinary tumor board.
* At least 1 tumor ≥ 2 cm and deemed to benefit from Y90 radioembolization by the institutional multidisciplinary tumor board.
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤2 (Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) ≥60%)
* Life expectancy ≥6 months, as determined by the investigator.

Exclusion Criteria:

All subjects meeting any of the exclusion criteria at baseline will be excluded from study participation.

* Definite liver transplant candidate
* Concurrent secondary malignancy
* Distant metastasis
